summary: Describes how SNMP messages are processed and dispatched within the SNMP architecture. It covers sending messages of different versions to the right message processing model and PDUs to the right applications, and defines the SNMPv3 message processing model. It replaces an earlier specification.

eli5.summary: When mail arrives at a big office, someone must sort it and send each piece to the right desk. This note describes that mail-sorting step for network-management messages.

subtitle: How an SNMP engine sorts outgoing and incoming management messages, and the message format SNMPv3 uses.

tldr.problem: An SNMP engine may have to handle several versions of SNMP messages and hand PDUs to several different applications, and each message needs the right security treatment.
tldr.mechanism: A single Dispatcher passes messages to a version-specific Message Processing Model, which works with the Security Subsystem, and then routes each PDU to the application registered for its contextEngineID and PDU type. The RFC also defines the SNMPv3 message format and its Message Processing Model.
tldr.outcome: It is an Internet Standard (STD 62) that obsoletes RFC 2572 and is updated by RFC 5590.

today: RFC 3412 is an Internet Standard (STD 62) published in December 2002. It obsoletes RFC 2572 and is updated by RFC 5590.

sections.title: The Dispatcher and Message Processing
sections.content:
The SNMP architecture in RFC 3411 says an SNMP engine is made of four parts: a Dispatcher, a Message Processing Subsystem, a Security Subsystem and an Access Control Subsystem. Applications use the services of these subsystems. This RFC describes the Dispatcher and the Message Processing Subsystem.

The Dispatcher sends and receives SNMP messages and hands PDUs to SNMP applications. When a message has to be built or taken apart, it delegates the job to a version-specific Message Processing Model. That model also coordinates with the Security Subsystem so that the right security is applied to the message.

The interactions are described with abstract data elements and abstract service primitives, which are descriptions of what information is passed and not a required programming interface.
sections.eli5: The mailroom has one head clerk, the Dispatcher. For each kind of letter the clerk asks a specialist to wrap or unwrap it, and then delivers it to the right desk.

sections.title: Roles of the Dispatcher and the Message Processing Subsystem
sections.content:
There is only one Dispatcher in an SNMP engine. For an outgoing message, an application supplies the PDU, the data needed to build the message, and the Message Processing Model to use. The Dispatcher has the message prepared and then sends it. For an incoming message, the Dispatcher works out the SNMP version, passes the message to the matching model to extract its components and handle security, and afterwards the PDU Dispatcher decides which application, if any, gets the PDU.

The Dispatcher also keeps statistics about the messages it handles in managed objects, so that remote SNMP entities can read them.

The Message Processing Subsystem holds one or more models. This RFC describes one, the SNMPv3 model, in its own section to show that independent models can exist at the same time and can be described in other documents. It names the SNMPv1 message format and the SNMPv2c message format as two models expected to be developed later.
sections.eli5: The mailroom can have several specialists, one for each kind of envelope. This note describes just one of them, the newest kind, and leaves room for others.

sections.title: Dispatcher Procedures for Sending and Receiving
sections.content:
To send a request or notification, an application calls sendPdu with the transport domain and address, the message processing model, security model, security name, security level, context, PDU version and PDU. If the model is unknown, an error goes back to the application. Otherwise the Dispatcher generates a sendPduHandle (unique across all models and of local significance only), calls prepareOutgoingMessage on the chosen model, and sends the result. A response goes out through returnResponsePdu and prepareResponseMessage.

For an incoming message the Dispatcher first increments snmpInPkts. It determines the version; if the packet cannot be parsed far enough, snmpInASNParseErrs is incremented, and if the version is unsupported, snmpInBadVersions is incremented. In both cases the message is dropped. Otherwise it calls prepareDataElements on the version-specific model.

Dispatching of the PDU then depends on sendPduHandle. If it is <none>, the message is a request or notification, and the combination of contextEngineID and pduType picks the application that registered for it. If none registered, snmpUnknownPDUHandlers is incremented and an error response is generated. If it is not <none>, the message is a response and the handle identifies the application waiting for it; with no such application the message is discarded and the same counter is incremented.
sections.eli5: When a letter goes out, the clerk writes a tracking number on it. When a reply comes back, the tracking number tells the clerk who was waiting. A brand-new letter has no tracking number, so the clerk checks which desk signed up for that kind of letter.

sections.title: Application Registration
sections.content:
Applications that want to process certain PDUs must register with the PDU Dispatcher. They give the combination of a contextEngineID and one or more pduType values for which they take responsibility, using registerContextEngineID. They give it up again with unregisterContextEngineID.

Each combination of contextEngineID and pduType can be registered only once. If another application already holds the combination, the registration fails with an alreadyRegistered error indication. Parameters may also be checked, in which case a bad one gives invalidParameter. Implementations may let an application register for several values at once, for example all contextEngineID values.
sections.eli5: Each desk in the office signs up for the kinds of mail it will take. Two desks cannot sign up for the same kind, so every letter has only one place to go.

sections.title: The SNMPv3 Message Format
sections.content:
An SNMPv3Message is an ASN.1 sequence with four parts: msgVersion (set to snmpv3(3)), msgGlobalData (the header data), msgSecurityParameters (an octet string whose format is defined by the security model) and msgData. The msgData is either a plaintext ScopedPDU or an encrypted one carried as an octet string.

The header data holds msgID, msgMaxSize, msgFlags and msgSecurityModel. The msgID coordinates requests and responses, and a response copies the msgID of its request. It should avoid re-use of outstanding values, and a retransmitted request SHOULD get a new one. It is separate from the request-id inside the PDU, because the engine must identify a message even when decrypting the PDU fails. The msgMaxSize tells the receiver the largest message the sender can accept, and its minimum allowed value is 484.

The ScopedPDU holds a contextEngineID, a contextName and the PDU. Together the first two identify the context of the managed information. The v3 model requires the PDU to be one of those specified in RFC 3416. The v3 model does not interpret msgSecurityParameters; it passes them to the security model named by msgSecurityModel.
sections.eli5: The SNMPv3 envelope has a label with a tracking number and size limit, a note saying how secret it is, a space for the lock's own details, and the letter inside. The letter may be in clear writing or in a locked box.

sections.title: Message Flags and Security Level
sections.content:
The one-octet msgFlags field has three meaningful bits. authFlag and privFlag record the security level applied to the message, and the receiver MUST apply the same level. reportableFlag is a secondary aid in deciding whether a Report PDU MUST be sent. It matters only when the PDU cannot be decoded, for example because of an incorrect encryption key.

The security levels are noAuthNoPriv, which is less than authNoPriv, which is less than authPriv. The architecture requires authentication whenever privacy is used, so privFlag set with authFlag clear is invalid. The receiver increments snmpInvalidMsgs and discards such a message. The remaining bits MUST be zero when sending and SHOULD be ignored on receipt.

The reportableFlag MUST be zero for Unconfirmed Class PDUs (Report, Response and SNMPv2-trap) and MUST be one for Confirmed Class PDUs (such as Get and Inform). A receiver treats a wrong value as if it had the correct one.
sections.eli5: Two little checkboxes on the envelope say whether the letter is signed and whether it is locked. You may not lock a letter without signing it. A third box says whether the receiver should send back a complaint if it cannot open the letter.

sections.title: SNMPv3 Processing Steps
sections.content:
To prepare an outgoing message, v3MP generates a unique msgID, builds a ScopedPDU and fills the header. If no context is given, the contextName becomes the default context, which is a zero-length string. It sets msgVersion to 3 and msgFlags from the security level and PDU class. The chosen security model then generates the message with generateRequestMsg, or generateResponseMsg for responses. For a Confirmed Class PDU it caches the request details so the response can be matched.

For an incoming message, v3MP checks that it is a valid SNMPv3Message, and otherwise increments snmpInASNParseErrs. It checks that the security model is supported (else snmpUnknownSecurityModels is incremented), derives the security level from the flags, and calls the security model's processIncomingMsg for authentication and privacy. Then it parses the scoped PDU and works out the PDU type. A Response Class or Internal Class PDU must match a cached outstanding request through its msgID, or it is discarded. A response whose cached security model, security level, security name or context differs is also discarded.

When a problem is detected, a Report PDU may be generated. It carries the error counter as its only varBind, with error-status and error-index of 0. A Report PDU MUST NOT be generated unless the failing PDU is of the Confirmed Class, or the reportableFlag is one and the class cannot be determined.
sections.eli5: On the way out, the clerk numbers the letter, sets the checkboxes, and has the lock-maker seal it. On the way in, the clerk opens it, checks the lock, matches any reply to the original question, and sends a complaint note if something is wrong.

sections.title: Security and the Statistics MIB
sections.content:
The level of security actually provided is primarily determined by the security model and the SNMP applications in use, since v3MP only interacts with them through the abstract primitives. Applications have access to unsecured data, and should obey the security level and call on an access control model.

The msgID values MUST be chosen to avoid replay attacks. They need not be unpredictable, only non-repeating. If a message exchange uses noAuthNoPriv, a third party could spoof or replay messages. Internal Class PDUs, such as Report PDUs, at noAuthNoPriv open a window for such attacks. The RFC says that a receiver aware of the risk may accept them, because they can help discover engine IDs or detect misconfiguration at remote nodes.

The RFC also defines the SNMP-MPD-MIB with three read-only counters: snmpUnknownSecurityModels, snmpInvalidMsgs and snmpUnknownPDUHandlers. It says the objects are not deemed particularly sensitive, but access can be restricted with security and access control models.
sections.eli5: A letter number must not be reused, or someone could resend an old letter and fool the office. The office also keeps a tally of the letters it threw away, and that tally is not very secret.
